newsitem.title: USA: U.S. probe finds unsafe Chinese electrical goods.
newsitem.headline: U.S. probe finds unsafe Chinese electrical goods.

text.p: U.S. investigators found many of the small electrical products imported from China every year were labeled with fake safety guarantees, U.S. News and World Report said in its March 3 issue.

Problems were first discovered in 1993 by Underwriters Laboratories (UL), the largest U.S. product safety tester, which found counterfeits of its own safety seal of approval on Christmas lights made in China.

"Nobody's keeping a national tally yet. But last year, customs inspectors at the port of Newark alone seized goods worth $3 million that had been stamped with unauthorized UL trademarks," the report said.
The United States annually imports about $2.6 billion worth of small electrical goods from China.

The news magazine said U.S. customs inspectors confiscated power strips with six outlets that had dummy surge protectors and dangerous wiring. Extension cords turned out to have wire too thin to carry a normal electrical load, and plugs fell apart when removed from outlets.

UL has now adopted a holographic label which is harder to copy. It has asked Chinese manufacturers whose products it certifies to use the new labels on 15 types of goods, including extension cords, lamps, and fans.

Chinese officials are considering a request from the organization for authorities to inspect labeled products before issuing export licenses, as well as a request for information on the locations of offending manufacturers, the report said.
